candidates.title: Chemogenetic dissection of the H2O2–salicylic acid feedback loop in PTI and ETI evolutionary conservation
candidates.authors: Yiliang Chen, Siyuan Tang, Chuyan Xia, Qi Wang, Shihong Wei, Duoduo Guo, Jufen Yan, Kui Zhang, Gan Ai, Xinya Han
candidates.abstract: The signaling interplay between hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and salicylic acid (SA) is fundamental to plant stress responses, yet resolving their spatiotemporal dynamics in vivo remains challenging due to spatial ambiguity when using multiple probes. Here, we present RhCy-NI, a single-molecule dual-responsive fluorescent probe featuring orthogonal reaction sites for crosstalk-free detection of H2O2 and SA. The probe exhibits ~25-fold and ~250-fold fluorescence enhancements at 562 and 751 nm, respectively, with detection limits of 96 and 24 nM and high selectivity. Time-course imaging in rice under salt and cadmium stresses reveals that a rapid, transient H2O2 burst precedes SA accumulation. In Nicotiana benthamiana challenged with the Phytophthora infestans elicitin INF1, pharmacological inhibition and SA-deficient genetic backgrounds show that early oxidative signaling is required for SA accumulation, whereas SA sustains a secondary oxidative phase. Genetic analysis reveals that enhanced disease susceptibility 1 (EDS1) primarily supports SA accumulation, whereas helper nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors of the NLR-required-for-cell-death (NRC) family (NRC2/3/4) support both SA accumulation and sustained secondary H2O2 amplification. These findings establish RhCy-NI as a tool for resolving H2O2–SA feedback and implicate components associated with effector-triggered immunity in cell-surface-triggered defense. Interaction between hydrogen peroxide and salicylic acid is important for plant stress responses. Here, the authors develop a dual-responsive fluorescent probe that simultaneously resolves the two signals in living plants.

candidates.title: Photocatalytic radical hydrogenation of unactivated alkenes via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer relay
candidates.authors: Weiqiao Lan, Ziyuan Wei, Zhao Wu
candidates.abstract: Despite the ubiquity of alkene reduction in chemical synthesis, developing safe, general, and chemoselective hydrogenation methods that avoid pressurized hydrogen gas or precious metals remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a redox-neutral photocatalytic radical transfer hydrogenation strategy that addresses these constraints via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer (HAT) relay. This approach leverages a synergistic diaryl ketone–cobalt–thiol triple catalytic system to utilize naturally abundant γ-terpinene as a sustainable hydrogen donor. Driven by visible light, the reaction proceeds through a HAT cascade to generate a reactive cobalt–hydride species, enabling the efficient hydrogenation of a broad spectrum of unactivated alkenes—ranging from terminal to sterically demanding tetrasubstituted variants—under mild, additive-free conditions. The protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity, preserving sensitive functionalities such as aldehydes, epoxides, carboxylic acids, and Lewis basic heterocycles. The practical utility of this protocol is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis with low catalyst loadings, establishing a versatile and environmentally benign platform for alkene reduction. Cross-electrophile coupling between unactivated alkyl halides and alkynyl halides has long been challenged by reactivity mismatch and poor chemoselectivity. Here the authors report nickel-catalyzed crosselectrophile coupling enabled by a tridentate ligand that controls the sequence of electrophile activation, allowing direct construction of alkynyl–alkyl bonds.

candidates.title: Taming crystallization to achieve superior soft magnetic performance via fine nanocrystallines
candidates.authors: R. C. Sun, X. S. Li, J. Zhou, Y. Q. Yan, S. Y. Di, J. H. Luan, H. L. Peng, B. A. Sun, H. B. Ke, W. H. Wang, H. Y. Bai
candidates.abstract: The increasing demand for high-efficiency power electronics in emerging technologies such as 5 G and artificial intelligence is limited by the intrinsic trade-off between high saturation magnetic flux density (Bs) and low coercivity (Hc) in soft magnetic materials. Here, we report a rotational magnetic field annealing strategy for Fe-(Co)-Si-B-Cu-Nb and Fe-Co-B-P alloys that enables precise control of crystallization kinetics. The applied rotational magnetic field promotes dynamic structural fluctuations in amorphous precursors, enhancing nucleation while suppressing grain growth. Consequently, fine nanocrystalline structures with grain sizes of 1–5 nm are obtained, achieving a high Bs of 1.94 T and a low Hc of ~0.8 A m−1. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that rotational magnetic fields generate spatially heterogeneous fluctuations, facilitating dense and uniform nucleation. This work provides a pathway for designing fine nanocomposite soft magnetic materials through external-field-controlled crystallization. Researchers demonstrate that rotational magnetic field annealing controls crystallization to produce ultrafine nanocrystals, enabling soft magnetic alloys with both high magnetic flux density and low coercivity for next-generation energy-efficient power electronics.

candidates.title: DPI-score: a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived assemblies
candidates.authors: Niraj Bhujel, Nick Whyatt, Agnel Praveen Joseph, Jyothish Thomas, Luc G. Elliot, Tamilarasan Sabapathy, Jeyan Thiyagalingam, Sony Malhotra
candidates.abstract: Abstract Advances in cryoEM have led to a surge in high-resolution structures; however, model building and refinement at resolutions ( > = 3 Å) and in regions with variable local resolution remain challenging, making validation essential. CryoEM derived assemblies often contain extensive protein-protein interfaces, however, most existing validation metrics focus on density fit or overall geometry without directly assessing interface quality. To address this, we present DPI-Score, a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived complexes. The method uses only raw structural coordinates of interface atoms, without requiring engineered features, and achieves 87.53% validation accuracy. DPI-Score was applied to 29,120 interfaces from 6,011 fitted entries with resolutions worse than 3 Å in the Electron Microscopy Data Bank. Here, we show that DPI-Score provides complementary information to existing validation metrics and can identify interface errors in modelled assemblies that are not detected by density-based scores alone.

candidates.authors: Yizhi Wang, Li Chen, Qiang Huang, Tian Guan, Xi Deng, Zhiyuan Shen, Jiawen Li, Xinrui Chen, Bin Hu, Zhe Lei, Xitong Ling, Taojie Zhu, Zirui Huang, Deshui Yu, Fanyi Zeng, Yan Liu, Jiurun Chen, Lianghui Zhu, Qiming He, Yiqing Liu, Diwei Shi, Hanzhong Liu, Junbo Hu, Hongyi Gao, Zhen Song, Xilong Zhao, Lingchuan Guo, Chao He, Ming Zhao, Yonghong He
candidates.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. We introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, built upon the subspecialized dataset and developed through two synergistic pretraining stages: self-supervised learning on approximately 190 million tissue patches to build a cervical-specific feature extractor, and multimodal enhancement with 2.5 million image-text pairs, followed by diagnostic functions integration and downstream task enhancement. CerS-Path integrates eight functions—across morphological diagnosis, predictive analytics, and multimodal tasks—to cover the diagnostic workflow from biopsies to resection specimens. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate improved performance in cervical pathology in female patients, where CerS-Path outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across 26 of 30 diagnostic tasks. Furthermore, in multicenter retrospective and prospective validation across six independent cohorts of women, CerS-Path achieves up to 99% sensitivity for clinically relevant lesion detection with acceptable specificity across sites, highlighting its potential for screening-derived histopathology and suitability for integration into high-volume diagnostic pathways. Foundation models could be promising for cervical cancer screening, but have important limitations for their clinical deployment. Here, the authors introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, a self-supervised learning framework for cervical cancer pathology that outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across multiple diagnostic tasks.

candidates.title: Kinetic balancing for near-equilibrium growth of defect-suppressed lead bromide perovskite single crystals
candidates.authors: Xiao Zhao, Ziqing Li, Tao Zhou, Yingying Hao, Shimao Wang, Gang Meng, Yadong Xu, Xiaosheng Fang
candidates.abstract: Controlling crystallization pathways for solution-grown lead-bromide perovskites remains a major unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a ligand-regulated crystallization strategy that achieves near-equilibrium growth for lead-bromide perovskite single crystals. Such regulation mitigates kinetic imbalance during crystal growth, thereby suppressing non-equilibrium defect incorporation, improving lattice coherence, and facilitating spatially uniform crystal growth. This strategy is applicable to a representative set of lead-bromide perovskites. Specifically, the resulting CsPbBr3 single crystals exhibit a high resistivity of 5.1 × 1010 Ω·cm and carrier mobility up to 93.95 cm2·V−1·s−1. Reduced electron-phonon coupling weakens optical-phonon scattering and raises the effective thermally activated conduction barrier from 0.43 to 0.71 eV, extending stable bias operation from 40 to 200 V·mm−1. These advances enable sensitive and stable ionizing-radiation detection under both photon-counting and charge-integrating modes. Overall, this work establishes a general kinetic-design principle for defect-suppressed, near-equilibrium crystallization of lead-bromide perovskites, enabling reliable high-field operation for ionizing-radiation detectors. A ligand-regulated crystallization strategy achieves near-equilibrium growth of lead bromide perovskite single crystals, suppressing defects and improving quality. The resulting CsPbBr3 crystals enable stable, sensitive ionizing-radiation detection.

candidates.title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
candidates.authors: Heegeun Kim, Chiwon Shin, Seunghoon Bae, Kyoung-Ho Kim, Hong-Gyu Park
candidates.abstract: Abstract Bound states in the continuum (BICs) support high-quality-factor resonances embedded in extended spectra, and their radiation properties can be tailored through perturbative symmetry breaking and chiral engineering. However, because BICs are intrinsically delocalized states of infinite periodic structures, they typically require large spatial footprints. Achieving localized BIC modes while preserving radiation suppression and topological singularities, and simultaneously enabling chiral responses, remains a challenge. Here, we experimentally realize low-threshold BIC lasers localized at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains with identical bulk BIC characteristics but opposite chirality. The resulting interfaces and junctions host spatially localized states that exhibit optical spin–momentum-locked emission governed by the assigned chirality, while retaining intrinsic BIC properties, including narrow far-field divergence and pump-selective lasing localization. In addition, polarization singularities confirm the topological nature of these low-dimensional BICs, particularly the well-defined topological charge of the zero-dimensional junction mode. Coupling two zero-dimensional BICs further gives rise to bonding and antibonding supermodes, enabling non-Hermitian, chirality-locked behaviors. These results establish a route to compact, high-quality-factor photonic states with engineered chirality through dimensional reduction of BICs, without relying on defect confinement or band inversion.

candidates.title: Sensory cortical disinhibition underlies long-term fear memory in humans
candidates.authors: Joshua A. Brown, Yijia Ma, Yifan Wang, John J. Massa, Peter Kuan-Hao Cheng, Chaowen Chen, Mingzhou Ding, Norman B. Schmidt, Mohammed R. Milad, Jair C. Soares, Raymond J. Dolan, Chenyu You, Wen Li
candidates.abstract: Abstract How transient threats turn into persistent, long-term fear memories is a fundamental problem in neuroscience, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Early sensory cortex, traditionally viewed as a passive feature analyzer, is increasingly recognized as an active participant in fear processing. Combining high-definition α-frequency transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD α-tACS) with simultaneous EEG-fMRI (electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging) and transformer-based neural decoding, we tracked fear memory development across formation, consolidation, and long-term retention (assessed at 15 min, 24 h, and 7 days after fear conditioning). Spatiotemporal memory traces were identified at all three assessments, beginning at an early sensory stage (40–60 ms post-stimulus) and distributed across visual cortex and limbic regions. Conditioning potentiated occipital α-oscillation desynchronization, a marker of visual cortical disinhibition, which subsequently predicted the strength of long-term memory traces. Critically, targeted α-tACS over early visual cortex induced early visual cortical (V1/V2) inhibition, abolished conditioning-potentiated α desynchronization, and selectively disrupted fear-memory consolidation and retention while leaving initial acquisition intact. These findings establish sensory cortical disinhibition as a necessary mechanism for long-term fear memory in humans and identify early sensory cortex as crucial node for intervention of persistent maladaptive fear.

candidates.title: Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults
candidates.authors: Annika Bendes, Sophia Björkander, Maura M. Kere, Simon Kebede Merid, Ashish Kumar, Leo Dahl, Tess D. Pottinger, Zhebin Yu, Anna Gardell, Amelie Vogt, Changil Kim, Qiang Pan-Hammarström, Anna Bergström, Inger Kull, Anne-Sophie Merritt, Sandra Ekström, Alexandra Lövquist, Ben Murrell, Niclas Roxhed, Erik Melén, Jochen M. Schwenk
candidates.abstract: Abstract Although population-based studies of circulating blood proteins have provided profound insight into human biology, transient changes to time-dependent exposures often remain elusive. Here, we perform a longitudinal dried blood spot (DBS) self-sampling study in 808 young adults (aged 24–27, 64% females) from the Swedish Barn [Children], Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm Epidemiology cohort. In total, we collected ~2400 samples from 2020 to 2022. Each sample was profiled for SARS-CoV-2 serological, anti-interferon autoantibodies (AAbs), and 365 inflammation-related proteins. We subsequently linked these samples to registry-confirmed infection and vaccination exposures, physiological traits, genetic variation, and blood counts. We show that data-driven seroclustering captures the response to both infection and vaccination exposures, while stable AAbs against interferon receptors IFNAR1 and IFNGR2 associate with the duration of self-reported COVID-19 symptoms. Genome-wide mapping reveals 664 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) across 65 proteins, with cis -pQTLs associated proteins showing greater longitudinal stability.
